text:
maya: Quick triage ask — release queue currently has 3 dependency CVEs that landed in the staging bill. Need to bucket them by SLA impact, public exposure, and customer tier so we can pick target windows. Thoughts?

jonah: can you list the CVEs + services affected?

maya: yea pasted below. rough initial impact notes. happy to revise.
```
CVE-2026-0451 | high | openssl -> used by hosted API ingress (TLS) | potential client-facing exploit, public exploit PoC in the wild
CVE-2026-1022 | medium | grpc-dep -> used in Dedicated control plane (auth) | requires local auth chain to trigger, no public PoC
CVE-2026-2108 | low | tokenlib -> used in Private appliance management UI | non-exploitable remotely unless admin UI exposed incorrectly
```

maya: my suggested buckets:
- CVE-2026-0451 => P0 (customer-exposed; exploit code; hosted API -> emergency patch + hotfix roll)
- CVE-2026-1022 => P1 (high-risk for Dedicated customers; schedule next maintenance window, notify affected customers)
- CVE-2026-2108 => P2 (patch on regular cadence; include in next minor release for Private)

li: +1 on classifications. For 0451 we should do a canary on eu-west first, rate-limit TLS handshakes during rollout. Also double-check our KMS key rotation doesn't interact with openssl changes.

ashley: tagging compliance — @security-gov we need advisory text for customers and remediation steps. Also which customer tiers get proactive outreach?

security-gov: suggest notify enterprise + Dedicated customers proactively. For hosted free-tier, publish status page entry and mitigation steps. Provide recommended configs for on-prem customers to block admin UI if needed.

jonah: scheduling constraints: Dedicated weekly maintenance windows are Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Hosted emergency patch we can push asap but need DB migration freeze? Any migration for openssl?

maya: openssl bump is binary-only for the runtime image — no DB migration. Need CI perf runs and a quick smoke across long-lived connections (KV cache). Plan: build image -> run smoke -> canary 5% -> ramp 25% -> 100% over 4 hours.

deploy-bot: [deploy job queued] build/openssl-patch-1911002034 started by maya — CI running (tests: unit, smoke, perf-slim)

li: for grpc-dep (1022) let's aim for next Tue window for Dedicated. Add canary routing for control-plane traffic to fallback to previous version in case of auth regressions.

ashley: I'll draft customer emails for enterprise/Dedicated and a short status update for hosted users. Will post copy here for review.

maya: assign owners: openssl -> maya + eng-runtime; grpc-dep -> li + eng-platform; tokenlib -> ashley + eng-infra. SLA impact: openssl = potentially impacts 99.9 latency and errors so we mark as emergency with page policy.

jonah: any public exposure risk like blog posts/active exploit chatter? We should prepare short FAQ and mitigation steps if PoC spreads.

maya: yes someone posted PoC on a public repo this morning (caught by feed). I'm drafting FAQ. Also recommending a temporary rate-limit and WAF rule for ingress until roll completes.

security-gov: make sure we log all rollout steps to audit logs and retain change records per compliance retention. Also include CVE reference and mitigation in customer-facing advisory.

maya: thanks all. I'll update the rollout checklist and post follow-ups as we hit each stage. Will ping when canary is green. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: CI passed (unit + smoke). build/openssl-patch-1911002034 -> artifact ready.

maya: canary started at 1911002360 — monitoring dashboards: https://console.internal/redwood/rollouts/1911002034

li: canary looks stable for 15m, ramping to 25%.

jonah: rolling to 100% now. ETA 3 hours.

maya: closing loop — full rollout completed at 1911002599. No regression alerts. I'll open postmortem if any customer impact pops up.
